reason: The Hebrew text clearly portrays the Israelites as a collective people and nation, explicitly using the term 'עם' (am - 'people') and describing them with organizational markers of nationhood. Key evidence: (1) They are described as multiplying abundantly and becoming mighty ('וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ') until they fill the land ('וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ'); (2) They are organized with 'צִבְאוֹת' (armies/hosts), indicating military structure; (3) God explicitly covenants with them as a unified people ('וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם' - 'I will take you to me for a people'); (4) They are portrayed suffering collective servitude and receiving collective deliverance; (5) Moses and Aaron are commissioned to lead them as a nation out of Egypt. While genealogical descent from Jacob (Israel) is mentioned, the text emphasizes their identity as an organized people and nation far exceeding what would be considered merely a family unit or religious followers.
